title: state-backup.sh silently skips `git commit -a`/`-am` and `git -c … commit` → S61 crash-durability backup never created
mechanism: state-backup.sh (KIT-008/S61) is the sole writer of the .backup snapshots that state-integrity's auto-restore depends on. It fires on PreToolUse Bash for `git commit`, then at line 26 requires SPRINT_STATE to appear in `git -C "$repo_root" diff --cached --name-only` (staged) or it `exit 0`s with no backup. But `git commit -a`/`-am` stage tracked modifications DURING the commit — after the PreToolUse hook has already run — so `--cached` is empty at hook time. Result: for the most common commit form, no backup is taken; if SPRINT_STATE is later corrupted (the exact scenario S61 defends), state_integrity.py finds no valid backup → 'файл НЕ перезаписан, почини вручную' → unattended/auto-resume run stalls needing the operator.
evidence: Sandbox (env-clean temp repo): payload `{"tool_input":{"command":"git commit -am wip"}}` with SPRINT_STATE modified-but-unstaged → state/.backup/ NOT created ('NO BACKUP DIR confirmed'). Control: explicit `git add SPRINT_STATE.md` then `git commit -m wip` → backup SPRINT_STATE.20260702-112816-35865.md created. Source: /Users/Apple/.claude/hooks/state-backup.sh line 14 `case ... *"git commit"*) ;;` (matches -am) and line 26 `git ... diff --cached --name-only | grep -q 'SPRINT_STATE\.md$' || exit 0`. Corroborated by operator's own SPRINT_STATE note line 22: 'SPRINT_STATE стейджить ОТДЕЛЬНО от commit (иначе state-backup не увидит staged)' — a symptom of this staging subtlety, but the -a/-am hole is not documented as a durability gap.
why_weak: The kit treats state-backup as the durability floor for unattended auto-resume (S61+S67), yet it covers only pre-staged commits. `git commit -am` / `git -c ... commit` are routine, and the auto-resume desktop consumer prompt tells fresh sessions to 'обновляя SPRINT_STATE per-task' with no instruction to stage it separately — so the durability guarantee is silently off for the common path. Not in kit-weakpoints/op-detect backlog (those cover the money-gate argv class, not backup coverage).
proposed_direction: Make state-backup independent of the caller's staging discipline: on any `git commit*` in a repo with SPRINT_STATE, snapshot the working-tree file unconditionally (drop the `--cached` precondition), OR additionally detect `-a`/`-am` and snapshot then. Cheap and removes the staging footgun. Cross-domain: also relevant to architecture-reviewer (crash-durability contract).

title: Desktop scheduled-task prompt: git mirror in sync now, but no mechanical sync gate between mirror and live task
mechanism: The auto-resume consumer contract lives in two places: git mirror kit/auto-resume/desktop-task-prompt.md and the live task ~/.claude/scheduled-tasks/kit-desktop-auto-resume/SKILL.md (created via scheduled-tasks MCP). The mirror is the documented source of truth but relies on manual re-sync ('при правке — обновить и задачу (update_scheduled_task)'). Nothing enforces they match — unlike hooks, which have hooks-selfcheck + kit-inventory + the kit/↔~/.claude/ mirror.
evidence: Read of both files: the prompt body (ШАГ 1-3, gate path, 'act only on GO', last_task_sha hex-validation, no --resume, unset GITHUB_TOKEN) is byte-identical between kit/auto-resume/desktop-task-prompt.md lines 17-36 and ~/.claude/scheduled-tasks/kit-desktop-auto-resume/SKILL.md lines 6-24 — currently NO drift. But there is no check that would catch future divergence.
why_weak: Same class as the KITVCS drift the kit tried to eliminate for hooks: a live behavior-defining artifact whose git mirror can silently diverge. If someone edits the mirror's gate path or the 'GO-only' rule and forgets update_scheduled_task, the live unattended task keeps stale behavior with no signal.
proposed_direction: Add the SKILL.md body to a manifest/selfcheck comparison (e.g. hooks-selfcheck or kit-inventory diffs kit/auto-resume/desktop-task-prompt.md prompt-block against ~/.claude/scheduled-tasks/kit-desktop-auto-resume/SKILL.md and WARNs on mismatch). Low urgency — currently in sync.
